title: GPU Pool Liveness Ribbon & Burst Dialer — prototype and review
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: design a compact, glanceable health ribbon and an inline burst/auto-scale control (the 'Burst Dialer') for Dedicated GPU pools in the Redwood Console. The feature should make pool liveness, headroom, and short-term burst capacity configurable and observable from a single compact header so SREs and platform engineers can triage rapidly without drilling into full telemetry pages.

Scope: ribbon + mini-metrics (utilization, queue depth, KV-hit ratio), burst dialer interactions (preset and custom burst), graceful fallback hints, simple rollout state, and a compact cost-exposure preview. Must work in Desktop widths >= 1024px; mobile views will show a collapsed summary card (follow-up ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates ribbon states (Healthy, Constrained, Degraded, Recovering) with color, iconography, and tooltip content.
- Burst Dialer allows selecting Preset x1/x2/x4 burst or custom token-limited burst with a 'simulate cost' preview.
- Ribbon interacts with Autoscale policies: when a burst is applied it shows expected post-burst autoscale behavior and an estimated cost delta for the next hour.
- All labels and tooltips pass accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation tests.
- Telemetry hooks defined for button clicks, burst apply/cancel, and preview opens (minimal payload keys: pool_id, action, preset, estimated_cost).

Constraints and considerations: must not add more than two additional API calls on first render; design should accommodate a 'low-fidelity' data mode if the backend returns partial telemetry. Prefers reusable components from the console design system (Badge, Popover, Slider, Mini-sparkline).

Success metrics: reduce mean time-to-first-action (MTFA) in pool incidents by 25% in the pilot, and >70% of platform engineers report reduced context switching in the post-launch survey.
decisions: Use a horizontal 'Liveness Ribbon' placed directly under the pool header to minimize vertical navigation.
Health states limited to four canonical statuses to reduce cognitive load (Healthy / Constrained / Degraded / Recovering).
Burst Dialer implemented as a popover with presets and a custom slider; commits require a visible 'cost preview' step before apply.
Cost preview will surface a conservative estimate across 1h and 24h windows powered by a backend heuristic; label this as 'estimate' in UI.
Keep ribbon rendering resilient: if telemetry is partial, show summary score + info icon linking to full metrics page instead of failing.
Opted for inline minimal animations for state transitions (fade + width easing) to preserve perceived responsiveness.
Telemetry contract defined: pool_id, user_id (hashed), action, preset, estimated_cost_usd, session_id.
Accessibility: all interactive controls reachable by keyboard; color not sole indicator of state (icon + label present).

2025-02-02 — Samir Patel (PM): Flags dependency on ENG-76234 for short-term cost estimator endpoint. Also wants a non-admin safe mode where burst is suggested but blocked until approval.
2025-02-04 — Priya Gopal (Frontend): Raised concern about two extra telemetry calls per render; recommended batch fetch for ribbon+preview and a client-side cache for 60s.

2025-02-05 — Design review notes: UX okayed for visual language; small changes requested — increase hit target on burst presets, add inline micro-copy about autoscale interplay, and surface last-burst-timestamp in tooltip.
2025-02-06 — Security review (early): Confirmed no sensitive data in telemetry; recommended hashing pool names in logs and rate-limiting cost-preview endpoints.
2025-02-07 — Luca Ramirez: Updated prototype with accessibility tweaks and added keyboard walkthrough. Marked ticket In Review and asked ENG for a staging integration for user testing next week.
